efdb7b4a29894d53549664d58da5bbf165ee6e1a.body:
The 15:55 message's replaces names the 12:33 one as
"...PT.261111123313.-PO-01-1939" (its identifier: "...123313.PO-01-1939"),
so the 12:33 wind to 18:00 stayed standing and the band still said
"Wind until 18:00". idk() compares identifiers with punctuation other
than dots removed, in channels, changeLine and capRecord. On today's
data: ORANGE sea to 21:00, YELLOW rain to 18:00, wind row ORANGE
12:00-15:56, note "ended at 15:56". 390 and 1280, light and dark: no
page error, 0 under 11 px, no overflow.

3aff58a8e8510728909b011a201624d7eff7016b.body:
channels(t): when IPMA's newest message for a hazard is newer than the
open-data feed, its windows already run are drawn (cDone) in place of the
open data's, also when neither channel has anything left to run. Before,
the 15:55 message (orange wind 12:00-15:56) left the wind row empty, and
at 18:05 it showed the open data's 12:34-18:00. Tested with the message
written into the built cap.json only; the band never says orange wind
after 15:56. Unchanged on today's real data; 390 and 1280, light and dark.

02a9db205eeec4dc0509f10934ab16c92a520b62.body:

Beja's orange wind ended early at 15:56; Faro's red rain to yellow and red wind to orange,
to 18:00. Lisbon now: yellow rain to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00. The storm in observed
figures (26.2 mm hour, 74 km/h gust); CP's own notice (fact). Residents bars drawn from
15:00 (E.bars_from): IPMA's file restarts re-issued warnings at their new onset, so earlier
hours there read as zero. Editions 1-8 unchanged.
